leads_to.evidence: No license or required next degree exists. BLS says most fine artists are self-employed and many hold other jobs alongside their art, and teaching art in college usually requires an MFA.

nearby_pair.evidence: Both programs take first-year students. Academy of Art University in San Francisco has open admission and accepts anyone with a high school diploma or GED, and Berkeley admits freshmen into its art practice major.

school_matters.evidence: Schools that admit under a tenth of applicants pay only a little more than open ones. No elite employer pipeline exists: BLS says most fine artists are self-employed and sell their own work, so a school's name moves first-year pay very little.

who_is_counted.evidence: The big programs admit students straight from high school. Academy of Art University, one of the largest, has open admission and needs only a high school diploma or GED, so the numbers mostly reflect new graduates.

programs.evidence: Too few graduates were counted to give a reliable figure.
